name: PowerShell Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell to execute arbitrary commands and evade signature-based detection.
indicators: powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -EncodedCommand
IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString
System.Management.Automation.PowerShell
containment: Enforce ConstrainedLanguage mode, enable script block logging, isolate affected workstation.

name: Valid Accounts: Domain Accounts
tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
description: Adversaries compromise and leverage legitimate domain user or service accounts to traverse enterprise networks.
indicators: Logon type 3/10 with unusual kerberos ticket granting request (TGS)
Domain admin account active from non-standard internal subnet
Concurrent logon sessions across multiple domain controllers
containment: Revoke active Kerberos tickets (krbtgt double-reset), reset compromised credentials, terminate RDP/SMB sessions.

name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
description: Adversaries use SMB admin shares (C$, ADMIN$, IPC$) to propagate payloads across enterprise hosts.
indicators: Net use \\target\C$ /user:domain\admin
PsExec service installation (PSEXESVC.exe) over IPC$
High volume SMB port 445 traffic between internal workstations
containment: Block workstation-to-workstation SMB port 445 via host firewalls, restrict RPC access.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Adversaries encrypt data on target systems to interrupt system and network resource availability, typically as ransomware.
indicators: Rapid modification of file extensions to .lockbit, .blackcat, or .crypted
Execution of vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet
Mass file rename activity exceeding 500 files/min in user and shared drives
detection_sources: Volume Shadow Copy Service event logs
containment: Immediate network port isolation, freeze storage volume snapshots, invoke cold backup recovery.

name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
description: Adversaries attempt to access Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) memory to harvest plaintext passwords and NTLM hashes.
indicators: Procdump.exe -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp
Mimikatz sekurlsa::logonpasswords
PROCESS_VM_READ access right requested on lsass.exe by unprivileged process
containment: Enable LSA Protection (RunAsPPL), isolate host, perform domain-wide credential hygiene.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries exploit vulnerabilities in internet-facing services to execute arbitrary commands.
indicators: JNDI lookup strings (${jndi:ldap://...}) in HTTP User-Agent / URI headers
Anomalous child process spawned by w3wp.exe, java.exe, or httpd.exe
Outbound LDAP/DNS queries originating from web tier servers
containment: Apply vendor security patch, place web application behind strict WAF virtual patch, rotate server credentials.

name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
description: Adversaries configure scheduled tasks to execute malicious binaries periodically or upon system startup.
indicators: schtasks /create /tn SecurityUpdate /tr powershell -enc ... /sc onstart
Task creation under C:\Windows\System32\Tasks with hidden attribute
Task Scheduler Operational Log (Event ID 106, 140)
containment: Query and delete unauthorized scheduled tasks via schtasks /delete, inspect scheduled registry keys.

name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
description: Adversaries send targeted emails with malicious attachments to gain initial entry.
indicators: Inbound email with password-protected ZIP archive containing .vbs or .hta
WINWORD.EXE spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe
Attachment hash matching known Emotet/Qakbot loaders
containment: Quarantine malicious email domain-wide, purge mailbox attachments, isolate endpoint executing payload.
